issues.failure_explanation: The delta-function computation and (chain_rule) replace sum_j mu_j^2 delta(h(t)-lambda_j) by sum_j mu_j^2 delta(t-h^{-1}(lambda_j)). The correct identity is delta(h(t)-lambda_j) = delta(t-h^{-1}(lambda_j))/|h'|. With it, the factor h' = (lambda_max-lambda_min)/2 cancels and J = I with no contradiction. The paper instead blames failure of the absolute-continuity hypotheses of the cited chain-rule proposition, and presents invariance as specific to discontinuous measures. In fact the Stieltjes integral against the pushforward mu∘h is invariant for any measure. For continuous measures a factor appears only through the convention of pulling back the density. The 'contradiction' is therefore an artifact of an incorrect delta manipulation, not a difference between measure types. The final conclusion (no scaling factor) is correct, and the first, Stieltjes-sum computation supports it.

failure_location.quote: This may be the reason that \eqref{chain_rule} fails.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the explanation: state the pushforward/change-of-variables identity for Stieltjes integrals, and note that delta(h(t)-lambda_j) carries the Jacobian 1/h'. Drop the claim that the dichotomy depends on continuity of the measure.
issues.overall_effect: The explanation of why the error 'remains unchanged' and the continuous-versus-discontinuous contrast are unsupported. No theorem relies on the faulty diagnosis, because the correct invariance follows from the first computation.
issues.title: Spurious scaling factor blamed on the Radon–Nikodym chain rule; continuous/discontinuous dichotomy unfounded
issues.why_classification: Only explanatory text is wrong. The invariance result used by the main theorems is already justified, so a short local rewrite suffices.

issues.failure_explanation: Replacing A by sA changes log det by n log s, while the absolute error of SLQ is unchanged. Applying the relative-error theorem to sA therefore only guarantees error <= eps*|log det A + n log s|, not eps*|log det A|. If |log det(sA)| exceeds |log det A| (for example, log det A near 0 after scaling down), the guarantee for the original matrix is much weaker than advertised. The assumption lambda_max<1 is used in an essential way: log A is definite, the Hutchinson relative bound applies, and |tr f(A)| >= n|log lambda_max|. It is not a harmless normalization.

failure_location.quote: This assumption is mild since for any SPD matrix with $\lambda_{\max} > 1$, it can be simply scaled to have eigenvalues $\lambda \in (0,1)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retract the 'mild' claim. State that after scaling the guarantee is relative to |log det(sA)|, and restrict the claim for matrices with lambda_max >= 1 accordingly (or treat sign-indefinite log A separately).
issues.overall_effect: The theorems are valid as stated for lambda_max<1. The advertised coverage of 'any SPD matrix' with a relative guarantee for the original log determinant is not supported. This also affects the interpretation of experiments on real matrices that must be rescaled.
issues.title: Claim that lambda_max<1 is mild because matrices can be scaled ignores that relative error is not scale invariant
issues.why_classification: The theorems survive, but the advertised scope of the relative-error guarantee must be withdrawn or reworked. That is more than a trivial edit and leaves some matrices without the claimed guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation preceding the theorem requires rho^{2m} >= K/(eps*log(n-th root of kappa / lambda_max)), because the factor n cancels against log(kappa/lambda_max^n) = n*log(n-th root of kappa / lambda_max). The theorem instead requires a larger m (an extra log n/(2 log rho_2)). The optimization of the product mN over alpha was carried out for the n-free m with constant C, so the stated pair (m,N) is not the one derived or minimized. With nK the minimizer would solve the equation with nC. K_{rho_2} is also written with an undefined alpha instead of alpha^*. The stated condition is still sufficient, but it does not match the optimality claim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the factor n in the m-bound and set alpha = alpha^* in K_{rho_2}, so that the theorem matches eq_optimized_m and the optimization problem.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the stated m and N minimize the product (matrix-vector-product count) is not supported by the stated m. The Lanczos bound is needlessly conservative and inconsistent with eq_optimized_m.
issues.title: Theorem ours_updated: Lanczos-step bound has a spurious factor n and uses undefined alpha, inconsistent with the derived and optimized bound
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction restores consistency with the existing derivation. No new argument is needed and the rate and conclusion are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Let phi(a) = a-1-2log(Ca). For C>1, which is the typical case, phi(1) < 0 and phi(a) -> +infinity as a -> 0+. So the equation for alpha^* has a root in (0,1) as well as the intended root >1. The theorem only says 'If alpha^* = ...' and never requires alpha^*>1. For a root a<1 the derivation breaks: 1/alpha + 1/beta = 1 forces beta<0, and the allowed error budgets sum to eps(2-a)/a > eps. The Lanczos tolerance eps/a exceeds eps, and N is computed for a meaningless Hutchinson tolerance. The conclusion at level eps is then not supported. Existence of a root >1 for C<=1 is also not addressed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis alpha^*>1 (the minimizing root) and the condition C*alpha^*>1 / existence of such a root, or state alpha^* as the minimizer of the objective over alpha>1.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the hypothesis is satisfied by a spurious alpha^*, for which the probabilistic relative-error guarantee does not follow. Only the root alpha^*>1 (the minimizer over alpha>1) is covered by the derivation.
issues.title: Theorem ours_updated: alpha^* defined by an equation with a spurious root in (0,1); the requirement alpha^*>1 is missing
